Rule in use: strength over 6 months, stop 3 normal daily moves under the close. I re-test 9 versions every night; 8 pass tonight.
Past test, 80 large stocks together since 2016, five held at a time: 465 trades, 38% won. Winners averaged +13.3%, losers -5.4%, all trades +1.79% each after costs (S&P 500 over the same days +1.06%). Typical hold 17 sessions. Earlier half 2.31%, later half 1.27% a trade. Whole account about 16% a year against 14% for the S&P 500. Best trade +146%, worst -27%.
Caution: the test list is today’s well-known companies, which flatters the past. The paper record below, counted from now on, is the honest test.
FAIR TEST (whole market, collapsed stocks included, 2021-10-12 to 2026-10-19): this version PROVISIONALLY PROMISING. It passed in the newer half at the 0.8% cost. Live paper trades must still confirm it.
Paper record since this list started: 3 finished, 0% won, average -14.0% a trade after costs. Winners averaged none yet, losers -14.0%. Profit factor 0.00 (above 1 means it earns). Best -3.7%, worst -28.6%. Deepest fall of the paper account 8.4%. Under 20 finished trades: too few to judge. If every entry had been filled at the dearest price inside its buy range: average -16.2% a trade.
Costs in these figures: 0.8% a trade (3 USD + 3 USD fees on a 1,000 USD buy plus the spread), the same cost the fair test uses. Trades finished before 18 Oct 2026 were counted at 0.4%.
